subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: One Hundred Years of Solitude and Magical Realism
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: One Hundred Years of Solitude and Magical Realism.

hook.text: Gabriel García Márquez wrote a novel where ghosts walked alongside the living and nobody found it strange.

buildup.text: One Hundred Years of Solitude chronicled seven generations of the Buendía family in a fictional town.

discovery.text: Published in 1967, it popularized magical realism and changed how the world understood Latin American life.

twist.text: Márquez said everything in the book actually happened; Latin American reality was already magical.

climax.text: The novel sold over fifty million copies and helped Márquez win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982.

punchline.text: Reality was so extraordinary it needed no invention.

quiz.question: What literary movement did One Hundred Years of Solitude popularize?
